biggest_catch: Free Basic tier has limits — 'unlimited job applications' is a paid Pro feature, so heavy appliers may need the $14.95/mo upgrade.
catches: Free Basic covers browsing, saving, and resume upload; unlimited applications require WWR Pro ($14.95/month).
No salary-transparency mandate — many listings omit pay.
No payment handled by the board; offers are negotiated with each employer.
Tech-skewed categories; competition is high on popular roles.

c1.evidence: We Work Remotely's official FAQ lists 35,000+ jobs posted, ~1,000+ new listings monthly, and states 'browsing and applying for jobs is free for job seekers' — a live, provider-owned deal channel focused 100% on remote work.

c2.evidence: Official pages publish no fixed pay range — compensation is set per employer; framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official guidance: browse jobs by category, create a free account, upload your resume, apply per the employer's instructions.

c4.evidence: Official FAQ: 'Browsing and applying for jobs is free for job seekers. You only pay if you choose to purchase optional services.' A free path exists (Basic tier); paid tiers are optional.

eligibility: Anyone able to work remotely; categories include programming, customer support, marketing, sales, design, and more.
notes: Scenario: remote job board. We Work Remotely is a remote-only job board (operated by 37signals) with 35,000+ jobs posted and ~1,000 new listings per month; browsing and applying are free on the Basic tier. Note honestly: unlimited applications are a paid Pro ($14.95/mo) feature, so free-tier application volume may be limited. Pay is per employer and negotiated — variable.

steps: Browse remote jobs by category (programming, customer support, marketing, sales, design, etc.).
Create a free Basic account to save listings, upload your resume, and follow companies.
Apply per each employer's stated instructions.
Complete the employer's hiring process and negotiate the offer directly.
